Remove the hidden data in your photos and PDFs

Photos and documents carry details you can't see: where a photo was taken, which phone took it, who wrote a document and what was deleted from it. Unmarked shows you what's there and removes it.

Your files never leave this device. Nothing is uploaded.

    Options

    Done

    What Unmarked can't remove
    • What you can see. Faces, street signs, house numbers, reflections and text in the picture or on the page stay as they are. Crop or cover them first.
    • Your phone's own records. Your gallery, cloud backups and the original file keep their data. Unmarked makes a clean copy; it doesn't change the original.
    • Clues in the content itself. Writing style, tracked changes already accepted into a document, or a scan's visible stamps and signatures.

    What Unmarked does

    Photos and documents carry information you can't see on screen. A photo from a phone usually records where it was taken (often to within a few metres), when, which phone took it, and sometimes the owner's name and the camera's serial number. A PDF can carry the author's name, the app and computer that made it, comments and who wrote them, attached files, and even earlier versions of the document with text you thought you deleted.

    Unmarked shows you what's inside each file and makes a clean copy without it. It runs entirely on your device: your files are never uploaded anywhere.

    Unmarked makes a clean copy. Your original file is not changed, and neither is your gallery or cloud backup. Share the clean copy, not the original.

    How to use it

    1. Tap Choose photos or PDFs (or drop files onto the page on a computer). You can pick many at once.
    2. Each file is checked. Tap What's inside to see exactly what was found, from the most revealing to the most technical, and whether each item will be removed or kept.
    3. Choose any options (below), then tap Remove hidden data.
    4. Each clean copy is checked again to confirm nothing was left behind.
    5. Save or Share the clean copies. Several files can be saved together as one .zip file. In the Android app the save screen opens in the same folder as the original, and suggests a name like photo-unmarked.jpg so you can't replace your original by accident. Browsers save to their usual download folder.

    On Android you can also start from another app: in your gallery or file manager, pick photos or PDFs, tap Share and choose Unmarked.

    Options

    • Keep the date taken: leaves the date and time a photo was taken. The time zone, which hints at where you were, is still removed.
    • Keep copyright notices: for photographers and artists who want their copyright line to stay with the picture.
    • Give files plain names: file names often give things away too. IMG_20261024_143512.jpg says the photo was taken on 24 October 2026 at 14:35. With this option the copies are called image-01.jpg, document-01.pdf and so on.

    Your choices are remembered on this device.

    Photos (JPEG, PNG, WebP)

    Removed:

    • Location (GPS position, altitude, the direction the camera faced) and place names
    • Names: author, camera owner, creator, contact details
    • Device details: phone or camera maker and model, serial numbers, lens, software and editing apps
    • Dates and time zone
    • Embedded thumbnails: a small copy of the original picture, which can still show parts you cropped out
    • Motion photos: the short video clip some phones attach to a photo
    • Edit history, document IDs and other data added by editing apps
    • Comments, titles, descriptions and keywords
    • Camera settings (exposure, ISO and similar) and other technical data

    Kept, because they are harmless and needed to show the picture correctly:

    • Rotation: so the photo appears the right way up
    • Colour profile: so colours look right

    Cleaning is lossless. Unmarked cuts the hidden data out of the file without touching the picture itself, so there is no recompression and no loss of quality.

    PDF documents

    Removed:

    • Document information: author, title, subject, keywords, the app that made it, creation and modification dates
    • XMP metadata, document IDs and edit history
    • Earlier saved versions: many apps add edits to the end of a PDF and leave the old version inside the file. Unmarked writes a fresh copy containing only the current version.
    • Camera data inside photos placed in the document
    • Page thumbnails and private editing data left by apps such as Word or Illustrator

    You choose, for each PDF that has them (all are ticked to start with):

    • Attached files: files stored inside the PDF. They can carry their own hidden data.
    • Scripts: code that runs when the PDF is opened. Rarely needed.
    • Comments and markup: notes, highlights and drawings, and the names of the people who made them.

    Kept: the text, pictures and layout, links, form fields and their answers, and layers.

    What Unmarked can't remove

    Unmarked removes hidden data. It can't change what anyone can see in the file.

    • The picture or page itself: faces, street signs, house numbers, car number plates, reflections, screens, and text on a page. Crop or cover them before cleaning.
    • Text that is in the document, including tracked changes that were already accepted.
    • Your device's own records: the original file, your gallery, and cloud backups keep their data.
    • Hidden layers in PDFs are kept. If a PDF has layers, Unmarked says so; check them in a PDF reader.

    Files Unmarked can't clean (yet)

    • HEIC photos (the default on iPhones and some Android phones). Most phones can save or share as JPEG instead.
    • Password-protected or encrypted PDFs.
    • GIF, TIFF, camera RAW files and videos.

    Privacy

    Unmarked has no server, no account and no tracking. The web app blocks every network connection, and the Android app has no internet permission, so it couldn't send your files anywhere even if it tried. The only things remembered on your device are your three option settings.

    The Android app

    The Android app is the same app with two extras: Share → Unmarked from any app, and saving and sharing through Android's own screens. Download it from unmarked.anonacondacodelab.com/android.html (not from Google Play; that page explains why). About → Check for updates tells you when a new version is out.
